_comment: Proof cells for the gf180mcu DRC bring-up (issue #15), and what each one
is expected to make `klt drc` say. run_drc.py runs every cell listed here
and FAILS the run if the report's rule_counts do not match `expect`
exactly -- that assertion is the whole point: it is what distinguishes a
green bring-up from a DRC pass that never checked anything.
generator  script that (re)builds `gds`, run with an interpreter that
has the pip `klayout` package. Committed alongside the GDS so
the proof survives an upstream deck change.
gds        committed GDSII stream, byte-reproducible (the generators
below is a real integrity check.
expect     exact {rule id: count} the JSON report's `rule_counts` must
equal. `{}` means the report must be status=clean.
expect_status  redundant with `expect` but stated so a reader does not
Keep `expect` in sync with each generator's SEEDED_VIOLATIONS dict.

cells.name: sw_unit
cells.role: positive control -- a single switch device on the four covered layers, carrying two seeded violations

cells.name: uncovered_layer_probe
cells.role: negative control -- grossly illegal geometry drawn only on layers the deck has no rules for; 'clean' here is the coverage gap, not a pass
